nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used a multivariate linear regression model with polynomial (quadratic) age terms. The normative model was: GMV ~ gender + TIV + age + age². The optimal polynomial degree was determined via BIC (Bayesian Information Criterion), which indicated that the model with the highest order of age being 2 was the best fit.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To account for the typical development of gray matter volume (GMV), we fitted a multivariate linear regression model for the regional GMV by age, gender and TIV using the controls. There were four options for the highest order of age in the regression model: 1, 2, 3, and 4. Through BIC (Bayesian Information Criterion), we found that the model was the best when the highest order of age was 2

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Gray matter volume (GMV) from 140 brain regions extracted using the AAL3 (Automated Anatomical Labelling 3) atlas, excluding cerebellum and vermis. Data were preprocessed using CAT12 with VBM (voxel-based morphometry) and smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: Voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was used to compute gray matter volume (GMV). ... The automated anatomical labelling 3 (AAL3) atlas (Rolls et al., 2020) was used to extract gray matter volumes of 140 brain regions excluding the cerebellum and the vermis

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included age (linear), age² (quadratic), gender (sex), and total intracranial volume (TIV) as explanatory variables. The model was fitted using typically developing controls (N=1146).
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we fitted a multivariate linear regression model for the regional GMV by age, gender and TIV using the controls. ... GMV ~ gender+TIV+age+age²
